\chapter{Boolean Analysis --- Tensorization}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomVariables.Tensorization
\section{Overview}
Minkowski for nonnegative product integrals compares mixed norms. Affine contraction for each of two probability laws then passes to their independent sum, including essential-supremum exponents.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Minkowski for nonnegative product integrals]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Tensorization.lintegral_minkowski}
\leanok
\difficulty{6}
Let $(A,\mu)$ and $(B,\nu)$ be probability spaces, let $f:A\times B\to[0,\infty]$ be measurable, and let $r\ge1$. Then $(\int_B(\int_A f(x,y)\,d\mu(x))^r\,d\nu(y))^{1/r}\le\int_A(\int_B f(x,y)^r\,d\nu(y))^{1/r}\,d\mu(x)$, with nonnegative extended integrals.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Comparison of mixed nonnegative norms]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Tensorization.mixed_lintegral_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Tensorization.lintegral_minkowski}
\difficulty{4}
Let $(A,\mu)$ and $(B,\nu)$ be probability spaces, let $g:A\times B\to[0,\infty]$ be measurable, and let $0<p\le q<\infty$. Then $(\int_B(\int_A g^p\,d\mu)^{q/p}\,d\nu)^{1/q}\le(\int_A(\int_B g^q\,d\nu)^{p/q}\,d\mu)^{1/p}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Affine sum contraction at finite exponents]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Tensorization.affine_sum_le_of_ne_top}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Tensorization.mixed_lintegral_le}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\mu,\nu$ be probability measures on $\bbr$, $1\le p\le q<\infty$, and $\rho\in\bbr$. Suppose $\|a+\rho bx\|_{L^q(\theta)}\le\|a+bx\|_{L^p(\theta)}$ for every $a,b\in\bbr$ and each $\theta\in\{\mu,\nu\}$. Then $\|a+\rho b(x+y)\|_{L^q(\mu\times\nu)}\le\|a+b(x+y)\|_{L^p(\mu\times\nu)}$ for every $a,b$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform moment bounds imply essential boundedness]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Tensorization.eLpNorm_top_le_of_forall_nat}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $f$ be an almost everywhere strongly measurable real function on an arbitrary measure space $(A,\mu)$, let $C\in[0,\infty]$ and $N\in\mathbb N$. If $\|f\|_n\le C$ for every integer $n\ge N$, then $\|f\|_\infty\le C$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Affine sum contraction at extended exponents]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Tensorization.affine_sum_le}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Tensorization.affine_sum_le_of_ne_top, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Tensorization.eLpNorm_top_le_of_forall_nat}
\difficulty{6}
Let $\mu,\nu$ be probability measures on $\bbr$, $1\le p\le q\le\infty$, and $\rho\in\bbr$. Suppose $\|a+\rho bx\|_{L^q(\theta)}\le\|a+bx\|_{L^p(\theta)}$ for every $a,b\in\bbr$ and each $\theta\in\{\mu,\nu\}$. Then $\|a+\rho b(x+y)\|_{L^q(\mu\times\nu)}\le\|a+b(x+y)\|_{L^p(\mu\times\nu)}$ for every $a,b$, with the essential supremum at infinity.
\end{theorem}
